hypothesisFromLead.statement: a grant minted once and cached (static/@BeforeAll/shared ObservedPublicationFixture state or a context-cached bean) ages past the 30s window in a long suite
evidence: ObservedReplayAuthorizer.authorize mints issuedAt=clock.instant(), expiresAt=issuedAt+authorizationTtlMs (30000) on every call; StudioService.executeTest calls it per execute; StudioAuthorizationIT.setUp calls executeTest per test. No grant is stored in any static, field, @BeforeAll, or bean.
ObservedPublicationFixture statics (CATALOG_JSON, POLICIES_JSON, SESSIONS cookie registry) carry no time component.

Clock injected in StudioAuthorizationIT's context is SchedulingConfiguration.schedulingClock() = Clock.systemUTC(); the only MutableClock beans are nested @TestConfiguration of StudioScheduleApiIT/SharedSchedulingIT (own contexts and own Postgres). All ReflectionTestUtils.setField(..., "clock", ...) sites target locally constructed objects, not Spring singletons.

Discriminator in main code: acceptCore -> ObservedReplayAuthorization.bind -> check(binding) refuses with GuidedSessionException AUTHORIZATION_EXPIRED (409) if expiresAt is not after the JVM clock, milliseconds before the INSERT in the same transaction. A grant that really aged past 30s is therefore stopped in Java and cannot reach the trigger. Run1 failed AT the trigger, i.e. the JVM clock judged the grant live while Postgres clock_timestamp() did not: a JVM-vs-DB clock disagreement, not an aged grant.

verified: macOS power log: host entered Sleep 2026-10-13 12:36:53Z and DarkWake at 12:50:01Z; second Sleep 12:52:35Z -> DarkWake 12:59:32Z.
Run1 class start timestamps show matching holes: StudioApiIT 12:36:33Z (0.54s) -> StudioAuthoringApiIT 12:50:02Z; LedgerStateMachineMigrationIT 12:52:38Z -> ObservedTerminalSettlementIT 12:59:33Z.
StudioAuthorizationIT started 12:50:06Z, 5s after the wake; StudioIdempotencyIT (same observed accept path) passed at 12:50:17Z.

Test DB is Testcontainers Postgres (jdbc:tc:postgresql:15-alpine, TC_DAEMON) inside the Docker Desktop linuxkit VM; the trigger compares grant times to the VM's clock_timestamp(), the JVM mints with the macOS host clock.
Trigger line 82 raises the same message for expiresAt <= clock_timestamp() OR issuedAt > clock_timestamp(); a DB clock behind the JVM by more than the mint->INSERT interval yields exactly this error.

Probe reproduction: JVM clock +2s and +788s (=measured 13m08s sleep) ahead of the DB reproduces the exact run1 signature (DataAccessException 'observed execution grant expired' ... 'studio_observed_execution_guard() line 82 at RAISE').
inferred: During 12:50:06-~12:50:10Z the Docker VM guest clock still lagged the host after the 13-minute sleep and was corrected by ~12:50:10Z (guest-stamped Docker VM logs are silent from 12:36:59Z and resume, correctly stamped, at 12:50:10.75Z; the last StudioAuthorizationIT test and every later class passed). Not directly measured: no guest-clock reading exists inside the failure window.

Supporting history on this machine (not this run): Docker Desktop's VM sntpc log (last active Dec 2024) recorded 5709 guest-clock corrections > 5s, all positive (guest behind host), typically hundreds to thousands of seconds, i.e. post-sleep lag.
